content: Reports of adverse events in patients taking perindopril, received since its market introduction, include the following conditions, though their causal relationship to perindopril remains uncertain: Cardiac arrest has been reported. Eosinophilic pneumonitis has been observed. Cases of neutropenia and agranulocytosis have been documented. Pancytopenia has been reported. Anemia, including hemolytic and aplastic anemia, has been noted. Thrombocytopenia has been observed. Acute renal failure has been reported. Nephritis has been documented. Hepatic failure has been observed. Jaundice, either hepatocellular or cholestatic in nature, has been reported. Symptomatic hyponatremia has been observed. Bullous pemphigoid has been reported. Pemphigus has been documented. Acute pancreatitis has been observed. Falls have been reported. Psoriasis has been documented. Exfoliative dermatitis has been observed. A syndrome has been reported that may include the following features: arthralgia or arthritis, vasculitis, serositis, myalgia, fever, rash or other dermatologic manifestations, a positive antinuclear antibody (ANA), leukocytosis, eosinophilia, or an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). For amlodipine, the following post-marketing events have been reported infrequently, with an uncertain causal relationship: Palpitations have been observed. Gynecomastia has been reported. Jaundice and hepatic enzyme elevations, mostly consistent with cholestasis or hepatitis, have been documented, with some cases requiring hospitalization. Regarding drug interactions: The pharmacokinetics of perindopril and amlodipine are not altered when these drugs are co-administered. No specific drug interaction studies have been conducted with the combination of perindopril arginine and amlodipine besylate, although studies have been performed with perindopril and amlodipine individually. Patients receiving concomitant therapy with mTOR inhibitors (e.g., temsirolimus) may be at increased risk for angioedema. For perindopril: Patients on diuretics, particularly those recently started on diuretic therapy, may occasionally experience an excessive reduction in blood pressure after initiating therapy with perindopril arginine and amlodipine besylate. Close medical supervision is recommended during the first dose, for at least two hours, and until blood pressure has stabilized for an additional hour. Perindopril can mitigate potassium loss caused by thiazide diuretics. The use of potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., spironolactone, amiloride, triamterene), or other drugs capable of increasing serum potassium (e.g., indomethacin, heparin, cyclosporine) can increase the risk of hyperkalemia.
